3. Short facts are that the present petitioner, Dhaka North City Corporation (hereinafter referred to as DNCC) filed the aforesaid Arbitration Application being No. 1 of 2021 before the High Court Division questioning the legality and propriety of formation of an arbitration tribunal, which was constituted pursuant to the Order No. 91 dated 5-11-2020 passed by the learned District Judge, Dhaka in Arbitration Miscellaneous Case No. 666 of 2007 and, also, the Order (without No.) dated 30-11-2020 passed by the Chairman of the reconstituted arbitration tribunal, Dhaka in reference to the above-mentioned Arbitration Miscellaneous Case asking the petitioner-DNCC to appear before it. 

 4. The Respondent No. 6, M/s Diba Enterprise, being the highest bidder in tender for the work of Management of Mirpur Bus Terminal (Popularly known as Gabtoli Bus Terminal), on 24-9-2003, entered into a lease agreement with the DNCC to manage and operate the said Bus Terminal for an initial period of 3 years as against payment of lease money. By the end of the three-year period, respondent No. 6 failed to clear his total dues and requested for extension of time and waiver of payment on the plea of force majeure situations, like Hartal, Strike, Eid, SAARC Summit etc. A Joint Committee was formed, wherein respondent No. 6 was included, who found that 257 days were wasted and DNCC waived Taka 45,65,434 and also gave an extension of 365 days to respondent No. 6 making the end date 30-9-2007, but respondent No. 6 failed to pay the dues of DNCC and the Government Tax and VAT within the extended time even. The petitioner-DNCC filed Certificate Case No. 775 of 2007 as revenue of DNCC and the Government taxes and, also, on 23-6-2007, invited a new tender to lease out the Mirpur Bus Terminal to private operators as the contract with respondent No. 6 was coming to an end. Respondent No. 6 did not take any step to pay the revenue due to DNCC and the taxes due to Government, out instead filed two applications on 29-7-2007 and on 16-8-2007 under sections 12 and 7A of the Arbitration Act, 2001 respectively in the Court of District Judge, Dhaka to stop the tender process. The application under section 12 was registered as Arbitration Misc Case No. 666 of 2007. Thereafter, on 4-10-2010 the learned District Judge, Dhaka appointed Mr Tofailur Rahman, a Senior Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, as arbitrator for DNCC and Mr AKM Faiz, an Advocate of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, as arbitrator for respondent No. 6, who then appointed Bangladesh Supreme Court's Senior Advocate Mr Rafiqur Rahman as the Chairman of the tribunal towards formation of the arbitration tribunal. Since the arbitration tribunal was constituted, the learned District Judge, Dhaka disposed of the said Arbitration Misc Case on 31-8-2015. In the meantime on 15-10-2013, respondent No. 6 wrote to DNCC requesting to settle the matter out of Court and to withdraw the Certificate Case No. 775 of 2007. DNCC being fair and cooperative gave respondent No. 6 a clean opportunity to settle the dues of DNCC and accordingly called a meeting on 13-7-2015. However, the out of Court settlement never reached any conclusion as respondent No. 6 did not agree to pay the dues. Suddenly, on 29-1-2019, respondent No. 6 filed an application under section 12 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 for re-appointment of arbitrators in the aforesaid Arbitration Misc Case by praying for restoration of the same. While the application for restoration was pending, the learned District Judge, Dhaka, vide his Order No. 89 dated 16-9-2020, substituted the heirs as the petitioners of the said Arbitration Misc Case and allowed the power of attorney in the said Arbitration Misc Case. Thereafter vide his Order No. 91 dated 5-11-2020, the learned District Judge, Dhaka appointed new arbitrators, and when vide Order dated 30-11-2020 the newly-formed arbitration tribunal notified the petitioner-DNCC about the formation of the fresh arbitration tribunal, it came to know about it on 7-12-2020 and approached before the High Court Division questioning the jurisdiction of the newly-formed arbitration tribunal. 

 11. In section 3 clause 11 of the lease agreement dated 24-6-2023, it is found that, there remains the Arbitration Clause, where it has been provided, inter-alia, for reference to arbitration consisting of arbitrators of whom the Petitioner and the respondent No.6 shall nominate one Arbitrator, in case of disputes arising between the parties thereto in connection with or arising out of the said contract. It was further provided that two of the arbitrators, appointed by both the parties, will nominate one umpire who will be the Chairman of the Arbitration Tribunal.
